records.quote: In economics and social sciences, researchers often use polynomial regression models
records.text: In economics and social sciences, researchers use polynomial regression models to analyse and predict trends (unemployment rates, income distribution). Remainder Theorem: quick evaluation of the model at a specific year, e.g. P(5). Factor Theorem: identifies when the model reaches zero. Synthetic Division: fast method to test values and simplify calculations.

records.quote: Let the quotient be Q (x) and the remainder bea x + b
records.stem: Warm Up problem: find the remainder when P(x) is divided by x^2 + 2x − 3, given remainder 3 on division by x − 1 and −5 on division by x + 3.
solution: Let the quotient be $Q(x)$ and the remainder be $ax+b$ when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2+2x-3$
Since the remainder when divided by $x-1$ is 3, $P(1)=3$
Since the remainder when divided by $x+3$ is $-5$, $P(-3)=-5$
Solving the simultaneous equations (i) and (ii) gives $a=2$, $b=1$

records.label: Warm Up
records.quote: A polynomial P (x) leaves a remainder of 7x + 6 when divided by
records.text: A polynomial $P(x)$ leaves a remainder of $7x+6$ when divided by $x^2-x-6$, and $4x-3$ when divided by $x^2+2x-3$. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2+x-2$.

records.quote: Explanation
records.text: Explanation

records.quote: Let the quotient be Q (x) and the remainder be ax + b when P (x) is divided by
records.text: Let the quotient be $Q(x)$ and the remainder be $ax+b$ when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2+x-2$. $P(x)=(x^2+x-2)Q(x)+ax+b=(x+2)(x-1)Q(x)+ax+b$ ......(i). Let the quotient be $Q_1(x)$ when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2-x-6$. Since the remainder is $7x+6$, $P(x)=(x^2-x-6)Q_1(x)+7x+6=(x+2)(x-3)Q_1(x)+7x+6$. Here, $P(-2)=-14+6=-8$. Also from (i), $P(-2)=-2a+b$. Thus, $-2a+b=-8$ ......(ii). Similarly, let the quotient be $Q_2(x)$ when $P(x)$ is divided by $x^2+2x-3$. Since the remainder is $4x-3$, $P(x)=(x^2+2x-3)Q_2(x)+4x-3=(x-1)(x+3)Q_2(x)+4x-3$. Here, $P(1)=4-3=1$. Also from (i), $P(1)=a+b$. Thus, $a+b=1$ ......(iii). Solving the simultaneous equations (ii) and (iii) gives $a=3$, $b=-2$. Therefore, the required remainder is $3x-2$.
records.notes: Printed worked solution to the Warm Up, with no 'Example' label; recorded as one prose block.

objectives.label: Find a remainder on division by a linear expression

objectives.description: Set out the coefficients, inserting zeros for missing terms, and bring down, multiply and add to read off the quotient and the remainder.
